posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
Before the sun fully cleared the horizon, Northern Cardinals were already establishing their claim, with sixteen detections logged before six. By the time the first Blue Jay landed on the probable tube seed at 07:26, Carolina Wrens were beginning their morning chorus.

The feeder station quickly became a hive of activity, with Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees accounting for the bulk of the 160 visits. This morning is significantly busier than the recent average, with 17 species detected so far compared to the usual eight or nine by this hour. A Red-shouldered Hawk called from a distance five times.

The visual log remains dominated by the small songbirds, with the Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees taking turns on the new tube seed. The auditory count continues to swell, driven largely by the Wrens, who have been heard over 150 times already.
